output.title: Spot free-tier limits before they interrupt work
output.body:
If you run a small business, one useful workflow decision is simple: do you know when a free-tier tool is about to stop being free? That can be a SaaS plan, an API, an email tool, or any service that quietly turns a convenience into a bill or a block.

The question is not “Can this tool do the job?” It is “Do I know its quota, and do I check usage before the limit is hit?” If the answer is no, you are leaving the timing to the vendor. That is rarely the best control surface.

A practical next step is to pick one tool in your stack and write down three things: the free limit, where usage is visible, and what alert or reminder will make you look at it. For some tools, a weekly calendar check is enough. For others, a vendor cost-alert email is better. Keep it boring. Boring is good here.

Why it matters: an unexpected limit can interrupt a workflow or force an unplanned upgrade while you are still deciding whether the process is worth automating. Early spotting does not make that decision for you, but it keeps it human and deliberate.

For a small team, that is usually the right test: first visibility, then automation, then approval.
